newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Saga moves closer to Santa Fe takeover.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Saga moves closer to Santa Fe takeover.

text.p: Norwegian oil company Saga Petroleum ASA said Tuesday its supervisory board has approved the proposed purchase of North Sea exploration group Santa Fe Exploration Ltd. from Kuwait Petroleum Corp.
The supervisory board met with Saga's management Monday night to discuss the deal, and final confirmation of Kuwait Petroleum's approval was expected soon.

Observers speculated that the deal was worth $1.2 billion (7.72 billion crowns). That would make it the largest takeover by a Norwegian company after Kvaerner's purchase of British conglomerate Trafalgar House Plc in April for 8.9 billion crowns ($1.37 billion).
"Saga will hold a news conference as soon as final clarification on the takeover is ready. The company expects a quick clarification," it said in a statement.
Market sources had expected Saga to make an announcement on Tuesday following the board meeting and after its shares were suspended from trading on the Oslo bourse a day earlier.
A purchase price of $1.2 billion would represent a 50 percent premium on even the most bullish estimates of British-based Santa Fe's value at between $700 million and $800 million.

Saga has long recognised a need to diversify out of the Norwegian sector of the North Sea, where about 95 percent of its hydrocarbon production is concentrated, to maintain its reserve base and remain competitive.
